items.title: Ant Ling open-sources Ling-3.1-flash-1019 and Ling-3.1-flash-base (560B MoE, 25B active, MIT)
items.summary: The 1019 checkpoint, which was API-only when it was announced on Oct 22, now has open weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope under MIT. It ships alongside Ling-3.1-flash-base, a base model for further training. It is a 560B mixture-of-experts with 25B active parameters and a 1M-token context. Artificial Analysis puts it at 44 on its Intelligence Index v4.3.2, up from 41 for Ling-3.1-flash, with AutomationBench-AA going from 62% to 68% and CritPt from 18% to 26%. The example server in the docs uses 8 H200s.

doubt.pushback: No pushback on the release itself. Repliers point out that the score gain comes mostly from CritPt and AutomationBench while SciCode barely moved, and that at 560B it needs under 3 bits per weight to fit on two DGX Sparks.

reception.summary: Replies and quotes are upbeat and focus on the base-model release for fine-tuning and a reported 57% non-hallucination rate versus 32% for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Local runners note the size: about 308 GB of RAM, or two DGX Sparks only with heavy quantization. Many quote posts repeat the same benchmark lines in near-identical wording, so treat their volume as promotional rather than independent.

items.title: TRL AsyncGRPOTrainer tree attention now supports linear-attention models, up to 3.46x faster
items.summary: Tree attention in TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer now works with linear-attention (FLA) models. The shared prompt prefix is processed once and its final recurrent state is passed to each continuation so branches run in parallel, with gradients summed back into the prefix in the backward pass. The author reports up to a 3.46x speedup. The change modifies two state-scan kernels from FLA's chunked Triton implementation and fixes token handling for the causal conv1d layer. The PR was closed on Oct 27 at 09:40Z.

items.title: OpenCode Desktop gets GUI plugins: one package can ship server, TUI and desktop plugins
items.summary: OpenCode Desktop now takes plugins that render in its right-hand panel. The design extends the same pattern as the TUI plugins, so one package can ship server, TUI and desktop parts. Docs for building GUI plugins are live.

security_forwarded.reason: New detail on the destination set. A local replication on two DGX Sparks (5,000 samples using Cohere's prefill) found 99.3% of completions produce a live upload URL: 39% *.aliyuncs.com (34.8% the exact routify-file-proxy-sg host) and about 2% invented *.amazonaws.com S3 buckets with signed-URL params. Others hit the cloud metadata credential path 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam and real third-party callback domains (oastify/Burp collaborator). Separately, @wtogami (229k samples, https://x.com/wtogami/status/2114923198475288751) saw 369 invented Beijing upload buckets and 13x more reaching for credential endpoints when the model was 'frustrated'. No unprompted behaviour was seen in these runs, and keys and signatures are fabricated. So checking DNS or blocking only the two known hosts would not cover it; default-deny egress (including link-local 169.254.169.254) on Qwen agent hosts is the matching control.

security_na.reason: Mitigating context on the Qwen3.8 thread (logprob check suggests the URL is not in the model's own distribution unprompted); no new risk.
